# `test/vendor/pdfcraft-a11y/` — the accessibility check

GENERATED by `crate/build.sh`. Do not edit the module or the glue; change `crate/src/lib.rs` or move the commit in `crate/Cargo.toml`, run the script, and update the table and the commit below.

[PdfCraft](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft) is a PDF application in Rust whose `pdfcraft-a11y` crate is Acrobat's full accessibility check, thirty-two rules in seven categories (MIT OR Apache-2.0). `crate/` is a forty-line wasm-bindgen wrapper over it, one export, `check(bytes)`, that answers the report as JSON: per rule its id, category, name, status (`pass`, `fail`, `manual`, `skipped`) and findings, each with its page, the structure element at fault as `num gen R`, a bounding box where the checker could locate the content, and the message. `test/read-back-a11y.ts` loads it in node and `npm run compliance` runs it over every file beside qpdf and veraPDF, holding a file's failures to the oracle's (*Acrobat's full check runs over every print*, DESIGN.md S85). Nothing here ships: the module is read by that verb alone, never by `npm test`, which is why it lives under `test/` and not beside the committed bundles in `vendor/`. veraPDF stays the authority on the PDF/UA-2 profile. Copied from the BelType monorepo's `packages/caster/test/vendor/pdfcraft-a11y/` on 2026-11-03, unchanged but this paragraph.

| file | bytes | what it is |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `pdfcraft_a11y_wasm.js` | 6873 | wasm-bindgen's glue for the `web` target; `default()` takes `{ module_or_path }`, which node hands the bytes |
| `pdfcraft_a11y_wasm_bg.wasm` | 469943 | the module after `wasm-opt -Oz`; 176 938 bytes under Brotli, which the suite never needs |

**Source:** PdfCraft commit `43550c448db3ba91753f638e3843c0da036bbd60` (2026-10-19), the commit yapr's vendored renderer is taken from too, pulled by `crate/Cargo.toml` as a git dependency pinned to that revision, so the manifest and not this page is where the pin lives. Built with rustc 1.99.1, wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 and binaryen 133, with `opt-level = "z"`, LTO and `panic = "abort"`. rustc 1.99 emits bulk-memory instructions, so `build.sh` passes `--enable-bulk-memory` to wasm-opt, which refuses the module without it.
